title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: For all $k, r \in \mathbb{N}$ there is an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geq n$ and $\omega(G) \leq k$, there is an induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ with $\chi(H) \geq r$ and $\omega(H) = 2$.
context_text: This conjecture is the induced-subgraph analogue of a theorem of Rödl on non-induced subgraphs of high chromatic number. Its origin is described as unclear in the paper: it is attributed to Louis Esperet in [10] (Scott–Seymour survey, 2020), while a footnote states it first appeared in Nešetřil [6] (1979) attributed to Fred Galvin and Vojtěch Rödl.
paper_contribution: Disproves Conjecture 1.1 for all $r \geq 5$ by constructing, for every $n$, a graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geq n$ and $\omega(G) \leq 3$ such that every induced subgraph $H$ with $\omega(H) \leq 2$ satisfies $\chi(H) \leq 4$; the case $r = 4$ remains open.
notes: Attributed to Louis Esperet in Scott–Seymour [10]; footnote clarifies original source is Nešetřil 1979 [6], attributed to Galvin and Rödl.
paper_title: A counterexample to a conjecture about triangle-free induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number

title: Question 3.1
statement_text: Are there graphs with clique number $3$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number whose all triangle-free induced subgraphs have chromatic number at most $3$?
context_text: A conjecture (attributed to Esperet, and earlier to Galvin and Rödl) stated that for all $k,r$ there is $n$ such that every graph $G$ with $\chi(G)\ge n$ and $\omega(G)\le k$ has an induced subgraph $H$ with $\chi(H)\ge r$ and $\omega(H)=2$; it is the induced analogue of Rödl's theorem that large chromatic number forces a triangle-free (not necessarily induced) subgraph of large chromatic number. The authors disprove it for all $r\ge5$: for every $n$ there is a graph with $\chi(G)\ge n$ and $\omega(G)\le3$ all of whose triangle-free induced subgraphs have chromatic number at most $4$. The case $r\le3$ holds, since by Scott and Seymour graphs with no induced odd cycle of length at least $5$ have chromatic number bounded by a function of the clique number, so every graph of large chromatic number with bounded clique number contains an induced odd cycle of length at least $5$ (triangle-free with chromatic number $3$). Thus $r=4$ is the only open case, and this question, first asked by James Davies, asks whether it fails as well (with clique number $3$).
notes: First asked by James Davies (private communication), as acknowledged in the paper.
paper_title: A counterexample to a conjecture about triangle-free induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number

title: Question 3.2
statement_text: Is there a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every digraph $D$ with no induced directed cycle of odd length, we have $\vec{\chi}(D) \leq f(\omega(D))$?
context_text: Digraphs are simple: between two distinct vertices there is at most one arc, in one direction (no digons). The clique number $\omega(D)$ is that of the underlying undirected graph. A $k$-dicolouring of $D$ partitions $V(D)$ into $k$ sets each inducing an acyclic subdigraph, and the dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)$ is the least such $k$. For undirected graphs, Scott and Seymour proved that excluding induced odd cycles of length at least $5$ bounds the chromatic number by a function of the clique number. The authors show the directed analogue fails: for every $n$ there is a digraph with $\vec{\chi}(D)\ge n$, $\omega(D)\le3$ and no induced directed cycle of odd length at least $5$. This question asks whether excluding all induced directed cycles of odd length (including directed triangles) suffices. The paper states, in its final version, that the authors subsequently answered it in the negative (Carbonero, Hompe, Moore and Spirkl, Digraphs with all induced directed cycles of the same length are not $\vec{\chi}$-bounded).
notes: The paper states that Questions 3.2 and 3.4 were subsequently answered in the negative by the same authors in arXiv:2203.15575.
paper_title: A counterexample to a conjecture about triangle-free induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number

title: Question 3.3
statement_text: Is there a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every digraph $D$ with no induced directed cycle of length at least $4$, we have $\vec{\chi}(D) \leq f(\omega(D))$?
context_text: This asks whether the directed analogue of chordal graphs (digraphs forbidding induced directed cycles of length $\geq 4$) has dichromatic number bounded by a function of the clique number.
notes: Answered in the negative by Aboulker, Bousquet, and de Verclos [1] (arXiv:2202.01006, 2022), as noted in the paper itself.
paper_title: A counterexample to a conjecture about triangle-free induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number

title: Question 3.4
statement_text: For which $l$ is there a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every digraph $D$ with no induced directed cycle of length not equal to $l$, we have $\vec{\chi}(D) \leq f(\omega(D))$?
context_text: A more general question subsuming Questions 3.2 and 3.3, asking which forbidden induced cycle lengths force the dichromatic number to be bounded by a function of the clique number.
notes: Answered in the negative by the paper's own authors in arXiv:2203.15575 [2], building on ideas of Aboulker–Bousquet–de Verclos.
paper_title: A counterexample to a conjecture about triangle-free induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number
